meta.project: ADR Reader — detecting adverse drug events in medical text
meta.note: Model verdicts are real outputs observed during the Project 7 runs (1 = flags an adverse drug event). 'gold' is the dataset's true label. 'llm_extracted' is what the LLM pulled out, shown to expose hallucinations.

examples.text: RESULTS: Evidence of neurological improvement and rehabilitation potential after severe myelopathy due to intrathecal injection of doxorubicin.
examples.lesson: The hard trap: the 'improvement' framing fooled the domain model AND the LLM — but the simple keyword model caught the harm. Even the best model slips on tricky sentences.

examples.text: Hepatotoxicity was observed in three patients treated with isoniazid.
examples.lesson: A clear-cut adverse drug event — all four models agree.

examples.text: Lithium was effective in reducing manic episodes, with no adverse effects reported.
examples.lesson: A clear non-event (the drug helped) — all four models agree.

examples.text: On cessation of the injections, the retrocorneal membrane grew rapidly to involve the entire posterior cornea.
examples.lesson: The LLM cried wolf — it flagged a harm with no named drug, contradicting itself and the label.
